All fat hate aside, what sewing machine do you use? Would you recommend it? I wanted to get into making my own clothes and designing some stuff but I didn't know were to start or what machine to even get.

I don't make or design full clothing myself. I do a bit of modifying to get clothes to fit and playing around, but nothing amazing or professional. If you want to get started, though, you probably need to spend around the $200 mark on a half decent machine. You could buy second hand or even rent if you need. That's far from the most you can spend and it should cover the basics. Buy a better one once you reach that level. Then you just start with simple stuff like a basic shirt and build as you gain confidence. There are a lot of sites that will take you through beginner projects and it's really not that hard.

I like it because it's a project. I prefer spending the time fixing a shirt that doesn't fit over browsing endless stores for one that does.

I make some of my own clothes and I use a Singer Esteem II (about $130). Like carsandsarcasm said, there are a lot of good resources online for how to start making your own clothes and tailoring/altering the clothes you already have. It takes a lot of trial and error in the beginning to get something that looks decent, but once you get the hang of sewing it's a lot of fun. You can also learn different ways to sew seams that make them a lot more durable than what you might get off the rack somewhere. It can be a bit of an expensive hobby, but I've been building up my stash of supplies for a while. I recently bought a rotary cutter (like a pizza cutter but for fabric) and it's made the prep for my projects so much easier.

I feel like I look a lot more put together now that I can alter my clothes myself. A lot of the clothes in stores that fit properly around my chest are too loose around my waist, so I can take the waist in myself and have a shirt that actually flatters all of me
